html.30 の道＝<b>太い赤線・太い茶線・レギュレータの端子30（換装車はオルタの: The path to 30 = heavy red cable, heavy brown cable, regulator terminal 30 (B+ on the alternator for converted cars), tightness of the terminals. You need to follow it to the back of the car
html.<b>2つとも消えた</b> → 共通部分（バッテリー〜キー〜INTER、そして: Both went out → the shared part (battery – key – INTER, plus the ground on the return path) is suspect.
html.<b>キーOFF＝2つとも消えている。これが正常です。</b>キースイッチの接点: Key OFF = both out. That's normal. The ignition switch contact is open, and no power reaches the light blue wire to the instrument panel.
html.<b>キーON＝2つとも点く。</b>黄色い点が、バッテリーから車の後ろのレギュ: Key ON = both lit. The yellow dots go from the battery round the regulator at the back of the car, back to the front, through the key and on to the instrument panel. The warning lights coming on is the signal that "power got this far".
html.<b>キースイッチそのもの</b>が犯人（接点が渡っていない）: The ignition switch itself is the culprit (the contact isn't bridging)
html.<b>キースイッチそのもの</b>（接点の摩耗・キーシリンダーの空回り）。: The ignition switch itself (worn contacts, a key cylinder that turns without engaging).
html.<b>バッテリーのプラス（＋）端子に当てた工具の先が車体に触れると、その瞬間に工:
If a tool on the battery's positive (+) terminal touches the body, enough current flows in that instant to burn the tool. There is no fuse on this heavy cable. Before touching terminals or heavy cables, disconnect the battery's negative (−) terminal first.
⚠️ While you are looking for the cause, don't leave the key ON. If the contact points have stopped closed, current keeps flowing through the ignition coil and points and they heat up (if they stopped open, nothing flows). You can't see from outside which way they stopped, and the battery keeps draining meanwhile. Turn the key back to OFF when you walk away from the car.
html.<b>バッテリー上がり・端子の緩み</b>（いちばん多い）。ただしこれはセルも回: A flat battery or loose terminals (the most common). But then the starter won't turn either, so ① in the table splits it out.
html.<b>ヒューズを疑いたくなりますが、この症状ではヒューズを見ても直りません。</: It's tempting to suspect a fuse, but looking at the fuses won't fix this symptom. The red wire to the ignition switch branches off the supply side of the fuse (as the diagram shows, it doesn't pass through the fuse). The cross-check also confirms that "the warning lights come on even with F1 blown". It's exactly the same reason as in Part 1 (the charge lamp).
html.<b>同じ「30」が何か所にも出てきます。</b>これは部品の名前ではなく<b>: The same "30" turns up in several places. It isn't the name of a part but a number for the terminal's role: 30 = a terminal that always has power regardless of the key, 15/54 = the terminal power leaves from when you turn the key (the original wiring diagram uses these numbers too). So the three 30s in the diagram are all on the same single path. In the diagram above, only the places numbered in the original have a tag — where there's no tag, it isn't a terminal.
html.<b>片方だけ消えた</b> → 共通部分は<b>無実</b>。怪しいのはその警: Only one went out → the shared part is in the clear. Only where that warning light goes to ground is suspect (= the Part 1 and Part 2 stories).
html.<b>計器盤へ行く水色の線</b>の断線・コネクタ抜け。: A break in the light blue wire to the instrument panel, or its connector pulled out.
html.<b>車の後ろへ行く太線／戻ってくる太線</b>と、その端子の外れ・緩み。レギュ: The heavy cable going to the back of the car / the one coming back, and their terminals off or loose. They meet at regulator terminal 30, so if that works loose, all the power at the front stops.
html.<span class=\"pin-hot\">●</span>バッテリーは車の: ● The battery is at the front of the car (in the trunk), ● the regulator at the back (in the engine bay), and ● the fuse box, ● the key and ● the speedometer are back at the front. A path that looked like a straight line in the diagram makes a round trip of the real car. That's how "one loose terminal at the back kills the whole instrument panel at the front" can happen.
html.<span class=\"qa-h\">よくある疑問</span> <b>「エ: A common question "If they're out while the engine is running, that's not a fault." In fact it's normal. GENERAT. goes out once charging starts, and OLIO goes out once oil pressure rises (the Part 1 and Part 2 stories). This page only deals with no lights with the key ON and the engine stopped. If the engine starts, the surest check is two steps: "they come on with the key ON, and go out once it starts".
html.<span class=\"qa-h\">テスターを出す前に、1つだけ</spa: Before you get the tester out, one thing Pull the starter lever and see whether the starter turns. That alone halves the suspects (① in the narrowing-down table below).
html.① <b>スターターレバーを引く</b>（キーの位置は関係ありません）: ① Pull the starter lever (the key position doesn't matter)
html.①〜③の期待値は、手で書いた数字ではなく、この絵と同じ計算（通り道の到達性）から: The expected values for ①–③ are not hand-written; they come from the same calculation as the diagram (whether the current can get through). ① turns the starter first because it's the only action that checks "the battery and both its terminals" in one go = that's the only part the starter loop and the warning light loop share.
html.② キーONで<b>キースイッチの 15/54 端子</b>にテスターを当てる: ② With the key ON, put the tester on terminal 15/54 of the ignition switch
html.②で12Vが来ていて2つとも消えているなら、<b>水色の線か計器盤の中</b>を: If ② reads 12 V and both are out, suspect the light blue wire or the inside of the panel. If only one is out, the shared part is in the clear
html.③ 同じく<b>30 端子</b>にテスターを当てる（キーの位置は問わない）: ③ Likewise, put the tester on terminal 30 (any key position)
html.⚠️<b>オルタネーターに換えた車には、この「レギュレータの端子30」がありませ: ⚠️ Cars converted to an alternator don't have this "regulator terminal 30". The same role — the turning point where the heavy cable from the battery meets and heads back to the key — is taken on converted cars by the alternator's B+ terminal. Measure there instead (where the cables meet depends on how the conversion was done, so following the heavy cables on your own car by eye is the surest way). The shape of the path — "all the way to the back and then back again" — is the same on converted cars. What this turning point looks like on a converted car is drawn in the Part 1 extra, "The charge lamp won't go out: alternator conversion".
html.⭐<b>ヒューズを通らないのは、この赤線だけではありません。</b>純正の整備基:
⭐ This red wire isn't the only thing that bypasses the fuses. The factory service standards list by name "the circuits not protected by fuses" — five on the D model = charging circuit and charge warning light / ignition / starting / oil pressure warning light / fuel reserve warning light. ⭐ On the L model this drops to three (charging circuit and charge warning light / ignition / starting), and the two warning lights moved inside the fuses.
In other words, much of what's involved in "the engine starts" and "the warning lights come on" sits outside the fuses. The range the fuse box can't tell you about differs this much between models.
html.⭐<b>締め直すときに、端子の白や緑や青の粉を「絶縁物」だと思わないでください。:
⭐ When you re-tighten, don't take the white, green or blue powder on the terminals for "insulation". The factory service manual says it conducts electricity — so it creates slow leakage paths not only between terminal and cable, but between the terminals and between the cells. This is one reason a battery goes flat when the car isn't being driven.
⛔ Don't put grease on after cleaning it off (it reacts with the electrolyte and makes the same powder again). The factory specifies a thin coat of pure, sticky petroleum jelly. ⭐ And be especially thorough underneath the terminals — it builds up where you can't see.

html.このあと<b>「太い線」</b>と書くのは、<b>原典の配線図が、この電源まわり: From here on, "heavy cable" refers to the fact that the original wiring diagram draws only this supply section thicker than the rest. It is the section that bypasses the fuses and carries large currents.
html.このストーリーは <b>FIAT 500（D・F・L・R型）</b> の話です。: This story is about the FIAT 500 (D, F, L and R models). The wiring is drawn from the original 500 sources.
html.この先のストーリー → <a href=\"/wiring-journey-st: Stories further on → The starter won't turn (this story's pair; suspects below the fork) / The charge lamp won't go out (where GENERAT. goes to ground) / The oil pressure warning light won't go out (where OLIO goes to ground)
html.ついでに液のことも。<b>セパレータの上 3mm</b>（ふだん）〜<b>5mm: And a word on the electrolyte. The level should be 3 mm above the separators (normally) to 5 mm (when fully charged); check it every 1,500 km and top up with distilled water only. The specific gravity in everyday use is 1.23–1.25 (all from the factory service manual). ⚠️ Don't try to correct the strength by adding dilute sulphuric acid — what's been lost is water.
html.キーをONにしたのに、<b>GENERAT.（充電）も OLIO（油圧）も点かな: The key is ON, yet neither GENERAT. (charging) nor OLIO (oil pressure) lights up. That's the symptom on this page.
html.キーをONにしても、計器盤の警告灯が<b>1つも点かない</b>。電気の通り道を: You turn the key ON and not a single warning light on the instrument panel comes on. We follow the electrical path on a single diagram and narrow down where it stops.
html.キーを回すと<b>30 と 15/54 がつながり</b>、水色の線1本で<b>: Turn the key and 30 connects to 15/54; a single light blue wire goes to INTER in the instrument panel (= the one feed rail that supplies both warning lights; we'll use this name from here on). From there it splits to the two warning lights, which go down through terminal 51 (GENERAT.) and terminal 0 (OLIO) respectively.
html.キースイッチまでは無実。残るのは<b>水色の線1本と計器盤の中</b>（INTE: Everything up to the ignition switch is in the clear. What's left is the one light blue wire and the inside of the panel (INTER and the bulbs) → go to ④
html.バッテリーから出た電気が車の後ろを回って前へ戻り、キーを通って計器盤の INTE: Power from the battery went round the back of the car, came back to the front, through the key to INTER in the panel, and the two warning lights went down to terminals 51 and 0, closing the loop. Now start the engine. If both go out, charging and oil pressure are both fine.
html.バッテリーの<b>プラス端子</b>から出た太い赤線は、途中で<b>2つに分かれ: The heavy red cable from the battery's positive terminal splits in two along the way. This is not a screw terminal but a joint between wires. Straight down leads to the contact on top of the starter motor (Part 3); this story follows the other one.
html.バッテリー・プラスの太線・アースの帰り道は<b>生きている</b>（セルの輪はそ: The battery, the heavy positive cable and the ground return are alive (the starter loop goes through them). The suspects are from the fork to the instrument panel → go to ②
html.上の絵は<b>キースイッチへ行く赤線が外れた</b>ところ（赤い札の高さ）。<b: The diagram above shows the red wire to the ignition switch off (at the height of the red tag). Everything below that wire fades, and both went out. If the starter turned in ①, the candidates for the break are only inside the box:
html.上は<b>端子0から落ちる灰色の線だけが切れた</b>ところ（×印）。OLIO: Above, only the grey wire going down from terminal 0 is broken (× mark). OLIO went out, but GENERAT. stays lit — proof that the shared part is alive. This one diagram is the basis for the narrowing-down above.
html.分かれ道から太い茶線が車の後ろへ回り、<b>レギュレータの端子30</b>に着き: From the fork, a heavy brown cable runs to the back of the car and arrives at regulator terminal 30. From there a heavy red cable leaves the same terminal 30 and returns to the front — the incoming and outgoing cables share one terminal under one screw.
html.原典の配線図では、計器盤の警告灯は<b>どれも同じ水色の線1本（INTER）で受: In the original wiring diagram, the panel warning lights are all fed by the same single light blue wire (INTER); they differ only in where they go to ground. So:
html.図の点灯・色はすべて計算結果で、絵に合わせて数字を作っていません。 ⚠️「線が外:
Everything lit or coloured in the diagrams is a calculated result; no numbers were made up to fit the picture. ⚠️ The "wire off" diagrams are calculated as one wire missing, not as a contact position.
⚠️ The limit of this calculation: it has no notion of how "narrow" a path is (voltage drop from contact resistance). A loose terminal that has only narrowed the path shows as "connected" in this diagram. The warning lights use only a tiny current, so they may light even through a narrowed path — in that case the starter shows the symptom first (Part 3).
⚠️ The inside of the instrument panel (the INTER feed rail and how the bulbs are arranged) is an estimate that can't be fully read from the original diagram. It's drawn with thin internal lines to set it apart.
html.容疑者は<b>バッテリー本体・プラス端子・マイナス端子</b>。警告灯が点かない: The suspects are the battery itself, the positive terminal and the negative terminal. The warning lights being out is a consequence; the warning light side is in the clear → go to Part 3, "The starter won't turn"
html.戻った先は<b>ヒューズ箱の30</b>（ヒューズF1の電源側）。ここから太い赤: It comes back to 30 on the fuse box (the supply side of fuse F1). From here a heavy red cable branches off to 30 on the ignition switch.
html.期待値は原典（純正取扱説明書の配線図）と実車の挙動から先に書いたもので、計算結果: The expected values were written first, from the original source (the wiring diagram in the factory owner's handbook) and how the real car behaves; they were not copied from the calculation. A single ✗ means the diagram's data is wrong. The "↑ … in the same scene" rows read one and the same scene from another warning light or another load = they check whether both warning lights go out together or only one.
html.線の色は実車の被覆の色そのまま（ROSSO=赤・MARRONE=茶・AZZURR: Wire colours are the actual insulation colours on the car (ROSSO = red, MARRONE = brown, AZZURRO = light blue, VERDE = green, GRIGIO = grey). Yellow dots = where current is flowing now. Faded lines = where no power is reaching. Only the inside of the panel is drawn with thin, light lines, because its internal wiring can't be fully read from the original diagram (an estimate); this sets it apart from the certain lines.
html.電気は<b>一周の輪でしか流れません</b>。行きの道が生きていても、バッテリー: Current only flows round a complete loop. Even if the outbound path is alive, without a way back to the battery's negative terminal the loop doesn't close. A tester on the positive side reads a healthy 12 V, which makes it the most confusing form: "the power is there, but nothing works". Part 5 is the story with this return path as its subject.
